description: Harden the worker-vs-orchestrator control-plane boundary: deny worker Write to scripts/cam/issues/ (not just prd.json) and teach the planner to encode hand-file requirements as on-main oracles, never worker stories.

userStories.title: Extend worker-actor Write-deny to scripts/cam/issues/ via a structured deny-set
userStories.description: As the cam control-plane guard, I need the worker-actor Write-deny hook to block scripts/cam/issues/ in addition to scripts/cam/prd.json, so an implementer worker can never add/edit an issue file on-branch and collide (add/add) with an orchestrator-filed on-main issue (the CAM-162 failure).
acceptanceCriteria: When CAM_WORKER=1 AND CAM_SESSION is set, a Write/Edit/MultiEdit whose file_path is under scripts/cam/issues/ (any file in the whole directory, matched by *scripts/cam/issues/* suffix/glob since file_path arrives absolute) is DENIED. [oracle: bun test test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts]

The single hard-coded suffix conditional is converted into a small structured deny-set (case/loop over the two protected suffixes *scripts/cam/prd.json and *scripts/cam/issues/*) whose intent reads as 'worker-protected cam control-plane state'. [oracle: grep -q 'scripts/cam/issues' .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh]
The pre-existing prd.json worker Write-deny still holds with no regression, proven by the existing cases in the test file. [oracle: bun test test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts]
A worker Write to a path OUTSIDE cam control-plane state (e.g. under src/) remains ALLOWED. [oracle: bun test test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts]

A planner Write (CAM_SESSION set, CAM_WORKER unset) to scripts/cam/issues/ or scripts/cam/prd.json remains ALLOWED, and an unscoped session (CAM_SESSION unset) is fully unrestricted. [oracle: bun test test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts]
The fail-closed-without-jq behavior is preserved (static printf deny + exit 0 when jq is absent). [oracle: bun test test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts]

The deny logic is identical across all three synced copies: .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh, templates/.claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh, and the src/vendor/_generated.ts embed (regenerated by the build). [oracle: diff .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh templates/.claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh]

New test cases in test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts exercise the scripts/cam/issues/ deny path by spawning the real hook script: worker DENY, planner ALLOW, unscoped ALLOW. [oracle: grep -q 'scripts/cam/issues' test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts]
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check). [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh + templates/.claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh (dual-copy, per-file: CAM-123 lesson, both must carry identical deny logic), src/vendor/_generated.ts (do NOT hand-edit; regenerate with `bun run embed-vendor` after editing the hook), test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts. The write-guard lives in the `case "$tool_name" in Write|Edit|MultiEdit)` branch; today it does `if [ -n "${CAM_WORKER:-}" ] && [[ "$file_path" == *scripts/cam/prd.json ]]`. Convert to iterating a deny-set of two globs (*scripts/cam/prd.json and *scripts/cam/issues/*). Gotchas: deny keyed on CAM_WORKER=1 (implementer-only marker) PLUS CAM_SESSION, must not block planner (writes prd.json) nor orchestrator; file_path is absolute in production so suffix/glob-match; keep fail-closed-on-missing-jq (printf static deny) intact; whole issues/ directory must be blocked (the CAM-162 collision was the ADD of a new CAM-0164.json). Add new test cases mirroring the existing prd.json worker/planner/unscoped trio but for a scripts/cam/issues/CAM-XXXX.json path (spawn the real script via Bun.spawn, do not reimplement). Grounding: docs/adr/0036 decision (a). This story is the real mechanical enforcement (per issue gotchas).

userStories.title: Planner rule: a hand-file-via-/cam-issue requirement is an on-main oracle, never a worker story
userStories.description: As the subagent-planner, I need an explicit rule that a 'hand-file issue via /cam-issue' requirement is encoded as an on-main file-assert oracle acceptance criterion (verified by the reviewer's existing behavioral gate), never handed to a worker to satisfy by writing the issue file on-branch, so I stop emitting the malformed AC that caused the CAM-162 add/add collision.
acceptanceCriteria: subagent-planner.md carries an explicit rule, placed next to the existing requires:'operator' rule, stating that a 'hand-file issue via /cam-issue' requirement is NEVER a worker implementation story and must be encoded as a file-assert oracle acceptance criterion that verifies the issue exists on main (e.g. git show main:scripts/cam/issues/CAM-XXXX.json), which the reviewer's existing behavioral gate re-runs. [oracle: grep -q 'hand-file' .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md]
The rule references the on-main verification form (git show main:) so it is mechanically checkable by the file-assert oracle path. [oracle: grep -q 'git show main' .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md]

No new reviewer behavioral-gate code is added; the process fix reuses the existing file-assert oracle mechanism. At most one clarifying line is added to subagent-reviewer.md stating that on-main existence checks are legitimate oracle targets. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Any edit to a templates/-embedded prompt copy is reflected in src/vendor/_generated.ts via regeneration, so the embed does not drift. [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Prompt-only guidance (no planner-output unit test: an LLM prompt assertion would be brittle, per issue gotchas; the US-001 hook is the real enforcement). Files: .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md (cam-cli self copy, used by THIS planning session) AND templates/agents/subagent-planner.md (downstream-shipped copy, embedded in src/vendor/_generated.ts). These two copies already diverge substantially (cam-specific vs generic; CAM-123 dual-copy-is-per-file), so word the rule appropriately in each but keep the on-main-oracle principle in both. Anchor the new rule immediately after the `requires` operator paragraph (around line 65 of the .claude copy). Optional single clarifying line in .claude/agents/subagent-reviewer.md + templates/agents/subagent-reviewer.md that on-main existence checks (git show main:...) are legitimate file-assert oracle targets. If any templates/agents/*.md is edited, run `bun run embed-vendor` to regenerate the embed, then confirm embed-vendor:check passes. Grounding: docs/adr/0036 decision (b), issue ACs 8-9.
